boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Rhode Island School of Design
boards.description: Ten food-focused Providence destinations with currently published late hours; confirm service before heading out.

cards.title: Chinatown on Thayer
cards.subtitle: 277 Thayer Street, Providence
cards.notes: Check the day before leaving: the restaurant publishes midnight closings Monday–Wednesday and 2am closings Thursday–Sunday.
cards.short_summary: A Thayer Street Chinese restaurant with late posted closing times.
cards.evidence_claim: Chinatown on Thayer lists hours until 12am Monday–Wednesday and until 2am Thursday–Sunday at 277 Thayer Street.
cards.access_notes: Published hours: 11am–12am Monday–Wednesday; 11am–2am Thursday–Sunday. Recheck for holiday changes.

cards.title: Caliente Mexican Grill
cards.subtitle: 267 Thayer Street, Providence
cards.notes: Use the published daily 1am closing time as a planning window, then confirm availability directly with the Thayer Street location.
cards.short_summary: A College Hill Mexican grill that posts a 1am close every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Caliente Mexican Grill lists its Thayer Street location at 267 Thayer Street as open 10am–1am seven days a week.
cards.source_title: Caliente Mexican Grill — Thayer St. Providence
cards.access_notes: Published hours: 10am–1am, seven days a week. Confirm hours before travel.

cards.title: Fellini Pizzeria
cards.subtitle: 166 Wickenden Street, Providence
cards.notes: For a later Wickenden stop, aim for Thursday through Saturday, when the shop posts 2am closing times.
cards.short_summary: A Wickenden Street pizzeria with midnight-to-2am published hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Fellini Pizzeria at 166 Wickenden Street lists hours until midnight Monday–Wednesday and Sunday, and until 2am Thursday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Published closing: midnight Monday–Wednesday and Sunday; 2am Thursday–Saturday. Verify before going.

cards.title: Antonio's Pizza by the Slice
cards.subtitle: 256 Thayer Street, Providence
cards.notes: Choose Friday or Saturday for the latest listed window, and check the location page again before making the walk.
cards.short_summary: A Thayer Street pizza shop posting 2am Friday and Saturday closes.
cards.evidence_claim: Antonio's Pizza at 256 Thayer Street lists hours until midnight Sunday–Thursday and until 2am Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Published closing: midnight Sunday–Thursday; 2am Friday–Saturday. The page states slices and whole pies are available.

cards.title: East Side Pockets
cards.subtitle: 278 Thayer Street, Providence
cards.notes: Build a late stop around Thursday through Saturday, when the official hours page lists a 2am close.
cards.short_summary: A Mediterranean food destination on Thayer Street with 2am late-week hours.
cards.evidence_claim: East Side Pockets at 278 Thayer Street lists hours until midnight Monday–Wednesday and until 2am Thursday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Published closing: midnight Monday–Wednesday, 2am Thursday–Saturday, and 10pm Sunday. Recheck before departure.

cards.title: Baja's Tex Mex Grill
cards.subtitle: 273 Thayer Street, Providence
cards.notes: The location page lists the same 2am closing time every day; use it as a late-food option after confirming current service.
cards.short_summary: A Thayer Street Tex-Mex grill whose official listing posts daily 2am hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Baja's Tex Mex Grill at 273 Thayer Street lists hours of 10am–2am Monday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Published hours for the 273 Thayer Street location: 10am–2am daily. Confirm service before visiting.

cards.title: Haven Brothers Diner
cards.subtitle: 12 Dorrance Street, Providence
cards.notes: Plan for downtown evening service: the diner publishes 2:30am closes Sunday–Thursday and 3:30am Friday–Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A downtown diner trailer with the latest published closing times in this set.
cards.evidence_claim: Haven Brothers Diner lists its Providence location at 12 Dorrance Street as open 5pm–2:30am Sunday–Thursday and 5pm–3:30am Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Haven Brothers Diner — Full Late Night and Dinner Menu
cards.access_notes: Published hours: 5pm–2:30am Sunday–Thursday and 5pm–3:30am Friday–Saturday. Verify changes directly.

cards.title: Yumi Bar
cards.subtitle: 75 Fountain Street, Providence
cards.notes: Use Thursday through Saturday for the 2am listing; the official page also identifies the Fountain Street address.
cards.short_summary: A downtown food and beverage spot with 2am Thursday–Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Yumi Bar lists its Providence location at 75 Fountain Street as open until 2am Thursday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Published hours: until 11pm Monday–Wednesday, until 2am Thursday–Saturday, and until 11pm Sunday. Confirm before travel.

cards.title: Sicilia's Pizza
cards.subtitle: 181 Atwells Avenue, Providence
cards.notes: Check the takeout schedule first: it lists 2am closings Monday–Thursday and 3am Friday, with split Sunday hours.
cards.short_summary: An Atwells Avenue pizza restaurant publishing late takeout hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Sicilia's Pizza at 181 Atwells Avenue lists takeout hours until 2am Monday–Thursday and until 3am on Friday.
cards.access_notes: Published takeout hours include 10am–2am Monday–Thursday and 10am–3am Friday; review the page for weekend split hours.

cards.title: Pizza Queen Weybosset
cards.subtitle: 215 Weybosset Street, Providence
cards.notes: For the longest published window, plan Friday or Saturday, then verify that late carryout service remains available before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A Weybosset Street restaurant listing carryout until 3:30am on Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Queen Weybosset lists carryout hours until 1:30am Sunday–Thursday and until 3:30am Friday and Saturday at 215 Weybosset Street.
cards.access_notes: Published carryout hours: 10am–1:30am Sunday–Thursday; 10am–3:30am Friday–Saturday. Confirm before travel.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named RISD spaces for research, making, critique, exhibitions, and campus resources.

cards.title: Fleet Library at RISD
cards.subtitle: Roger Mandle Building, Providence
cards.notes: Use the main reading room to pull art and design references, then ask library staff for help locating specialized physical or digital materials.
cards.short_summary: A historic banking hall repurposed for art and design research.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says Fleet Library has more than 150,000 circulating books and resources in art, design, architecture, and related fields.
cards.access_notes: RISD identifies the library as a campus resource; confirm current visitor and borrowing access with Fleet Library.

cards.title: RISD Museum
cards.subtitle: RISD campus, Providence
cards.notes: Bring a sketchbook for a close-looking session, or check the museum calendar for lectures, concerts, and screenings before you go.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum collection connecting visual research with public programs.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD states that students have access to lectures, concerts, screenings, and more than 90,000 works at the RISD Museum.
cards.source_title: Academic Resources and Galleries on Campus | RISD
cards.access_notes: RISD lists it as a campus resource; consult the museum directly for current entry and program details.

cards.title: Co-Works Research Lab
cards.subtitle: RISD campus, Providence
cards.notes: Check current peer-tutoring or sponsored-studio opportunities when a project needs advanced tools or cross-departmental feedback.
cards.short_summary: A research lab organized around advanced tools and collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD describes Co-Works as a cross-departmental research space with peer tutoring, sponsored studios, and interdisciplinary collaboration.
cards.source_title: Academic Resources and Galleries on Campus | RISD
cards.access_notes: Use is tied to RISD programming and resources; verify current lab access and support offerings before visiting.

cards.title: Color Lab
cards.subtitle: RISD campus, Providence
cards.notes: Use the materials and object collection to compare color relationships in person, then translate observations into your studio tests.
cards.short_summary: A materials-focused setting for investigating color across disciplines.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says the Color Lab’s collection of materials and objects supports exploration of color across art and design fields.
cards.source_title: Academic Resources and Galleries on Campus | RISD
cards.access_notes: RISD lists the lab as a campus resource; confirm current access procedures with the relevant department.

cards.title: Movement Lab
cards.subtitle: RISD campus, Providence
cards.notes: Look for current experimental research or active-learning sessions if your work involves movement, performance, or embodied design.
cards.short_summary: A setting for research and exchange through movement.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says the Movement Lab supports investigation of movement’s social, cultural, ecological, and expressive properties.
cards.source_title: Academic Resources and Galleries on Campus | RISD
cards.access_notes: Programming and access may vary; check with RISD before planning a visit.

cards.title: Edna W. Lawrence Nature Lab
cards.subtitle: Waterman Building, 13 Waterman Street
cards.notes: Study specimens or imaging resources for a project connecting art, design, and science; arrange any requested room or equipment use in advance.
cards.short_summary: A natural-history collection and imaging resource for hands-on visual research.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says the Nature Lab provides advanced imaging systems and access to more than 80,000 specimens for design research.
cards.source_title: RISD Nature Lab Collections and Research Lab | RISD
cards.access_notes: The Nature Lab describes reservation forms for some rooms and equipment; contact the lab to confirm current availability.

cards.entity_name: Studio for Research in Sound and Technology
cards.title: Studio for Research in Sound and Technology
cards.subtitle: RISD campus, Providence
cards.notes: Explore current studio or independent-research options when a project calls for sound composition, soundscape work, or acoustic simulation.
cards.short_summary: A hub for experimental sound work and research.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says this studio supports sonic experimentation, experimental music composition, soundscape design, and acoustic simulation.
cards.source_title: Academic Resources and Galleries on Campus | RISD
cards.access_notes: Studios and independent research are program-dependent; verify current access with RISD.

cards.title: Sustainability Design Lab
cards.subtitle: RISD campus, Providence
cards.notes: Use the lab’s low-impact design focus to frame material or site questions, and check for current projects open to student participation.
cards.short_summary: A lab linking interior and landscape architecture through sustainability.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says the Sustainability Design Lab develops low-impact design strategies and inclusive material cultures at the intersection of interior and landscape architecture.
cards.source_title: Academic Resources and Galleries on Campus | RISD
cards.access_notes: Confirm current lab programming and participation options with RISD.

cards.title: Gelman Student Exhibitions Gallery
cards.subtitle: Entrance to the RISD Museum, Providence
cards.notes: See a current student-curated group exhibition, then review proposal details if you want to develop a show with other students.
cards.short_summary: A gallery for student-proposed and student-curated group exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says students may propose and curate group shows at the Gelman Student Exhibitions Gallery, located at the RISD Museum entrance.
cards.access_notes: Exhibitions change; check RISD’s current exhibition information before visiting or proposing a show.

cards.title: Woods-Gerry Gallery
cards.subtitle: RISD campus, Providence
cards.notes: Visit an undergraduate exhibition to see how work is prepared and mounted, and watch for opportunities to participate in campus shows.
cards.short_summary: RISD’s primary venue for undergraduate exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD identifies Woods-Gerry Gallery as its primary venue for undergraduate work and says students gain experience preparing, mounting, and publicly sharing work there.
cards.access_notes: Gallery schedules change throughout the academic year; verify the current exhibition before visiting.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-cost RISD and Providence activities with publicly documented access or free participation.

cards.title: Sketch at the RISD Museum
cards.subtitle: RISD Museum · 20 North Main Street
cards.notes: Bring a sketchbook and meet up in the galleries; RISD students enter free with a valid college ID, and pencils and sketchbooks are permitted.
cards.short_summary: A collection visit that leaves room for a slow, self-directed drawing session.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD students always receive free museum admission with a college ID, and the museum welcomes pencils and sketchbooks.
cards.access_notes: For RISD students; bring a valid college ID. Check the museum’s current open hours before going.

cards.title: Pick up Loop Lab materials
cards.subtitle: Second Life Exchange · RISD
cards.notes: Submit the Loop Lab order form, then collect reclaimed paper, muslin, clay, or other available materials for a shared making session.
cards.short_summary: Start a small project with campus waste streams transformed into usable art materials.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD’s Nature Lab states that Loop Lab materials may be ordered free of charge and picked up at the Second Life Exchange.
cards.access_notes: For RISD students; submit an order first. Availability and pickup details arrive by confirmation email.

cards.title: Settle into Providence Public Library
cards.subtitle: 150 Empire Street · Downtown Providence
cards.notes: Choose a table, compare current projects, or read together in the public library; bring your own materials and respect library rules.
cards.short_summary: A downtown indoor gathering point built around free public library service.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence Public Library describes itself as a free and open place to gather and a provider of free public library service.
cards.access_notes: Public access is free; visit during posted library hours and follow onsite policies.

cards.title: Walk Roger Williams National Memorial
cards.subtitle: 282 North Main Street · Providence
cards.notes: Take a low-key lap of the grounds, pause by the historic well site, and use the picnic tables for a no-purchase outdoor catch-up.
cards.short_summary: A compact National Park Service site for a free downtown walk or picnic.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service says there is no fee or entrance pass required to enter Roger Williams National Memorial.
cards.source_title: Fees & Passes — Roger Williams National Memorial
cards.access_notes: No entrance fee. Park grounds are open daily from dawn to dusk; visitor-center hours vary seasonally.

cards.entity_name: Rhode Island State House walk-in tour
cards.title: Take a State House tour
cards.subtitle: Rhode Island State House · 82 Smith Street
cards.notes: Meet for a docent-led walk-in tour and look up into the marble dome; arrive for the listed 10 a.m. or 1 p.m. weekday start.
cards.short_summary: A free guided look inside Rhode Island’s State House.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rhode Island Secretary of State offers free walk-in general-public docent-led tours Monday through Friday at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Free walk-in tours are weekdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.; reservations are encouraged but not required for walk-ins.

cards.title: Join Wednesday Night Run Club
cards.subtitle: India Point Park · George Redman Linear entrance
cards.notes: Bring a friend and join the Wednesday evening run at India Point Park; the city lists no signup requirement for this recurring activity.
cards.short_summary: A city-listed, no-registration group run by the waterfront.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence lists Wednesday Night Run Club at India Point Park at 6 p.m. and states that no signup is required.
cards.source_title: Parks + Playground Programs — Eat, Play, Learn PVD
cards.access_notes: Listed for Wednesdays at 6 p.m. at India Point Park’s George Redman Linear entrance; confirm seasonal programming before travel.

cards.title: Try Tai Chi Paradigm Introduction
cards.subtitle: Roger Williams Park Gateway Center or Botanical Center
cards.notes: Join a city fitness class with a friend and move at your own pace; bring water and complete the required participant waiver before class.
cards.short_summary: A structured, gentle group exercise option in Roger Williams Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence identifies Tai Chi Paradigm Introduction as part of its Fitness in the Parks program, which it describes as safe and free for all ages and abilities.
cards.source_title: Parks + Playground Programs — Eat, Play, Learn PVD
cards.access_notes: A participant waiver is required before the first Fitness in the Parks activity. Check the city page for current location and schedule.

cards.title: Move through a barre class
cards.subtitle: Roger Williams Park Gateway Center
cards.notes: Meet at the Gateway Center for the listed barre session, then cool down together in the park; complete the city’s first-activity waiver.
cards.short_summary: A free city-led fitness class with a clear park meeting point.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence lists Barre within Fitness in the Parks and describes those classes as safe and free for all ages and abilities.
cards.source_title: Parks + Playground Programs — Eat, Play, Learn PVD
cards.access_notes: The city lists Barre at the Roger Williams Park Gateway Center; a waiver is required before a first program activity.

cards.title: Stretch at All Ages Yoga
cards.subtitle: Roger Williams Park Gateway Center
cards.notes: Bring a towel or mat if you have one and join the listed yoga session; the class is designed for all ages and abilities through the city program.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost group yoga session in a named Roger Williams Park facility.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence lists All Ages Yoga at the Roger Williams Park Gateway Center through its safe, free Fitness in the Parks classes.
cards.source_title: Parks + Playground Programs — Eat, Play, Learn PVD
cards.access_notes: The listed session is Wednesdays, 10–11 a.m.; a participant waiver is required before the first Fitness in the Parks activity.

cards.title: Get moving with Pep in Your Step
cards.subtitle: Roger Williams Park Gateway Center
cards.notes: Use the listed Thursday session as a planned movement break with classmates; complete the city waiver before joining your first park fitness class.
cards.short_summary: A free, city-run group fitness activity at the Gateway Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence lists Pep in Your Step at the Roger Williams Park Gateway Center as part of its safe, free Fitness in the Parks program.
cards.source_title: Parks + Playground Programs — Eat, Play, Learn PVD
cards.access_notes: The listed session is Thursdays, 5–6 p.m.; check the city page for changes and complete the required waiver before first participation.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented RISD environments for research, reference work, collaborative projects and visual study.

cards.title: Fleet Library Main Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Fleet Library at RISD, 15 Westminster Street
cards.notes: Set up in the former bank’s main reading room when you want to work beside the circulating art and design collection.
cards.short_summary: A historic banking-hall reading room for book-based art and design research.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD identifies the former bank’s main hall as Fleet Library’s main reading room and describes its art, design, architecture and photography collections.
cards.source_title: Fleet Library | Rhode Island School of Design Research
cards.access_notes: Located at Fleet Library, 15 Westminster Street; consult Fleet Library for current building access and hours.

cards.title: Fleet Library Study Pavilion
cards.subtitle: Fleet Library, first floor
cards.notes: Use the stepped pavilion for an informal work session; its tiers and adjacent work surfaces support varied postures.
cards.short_summary: A stepped work setting within Fleet Library’s main reading room.
cards.evidence_claim: Fleet Library’s architectural documentation says the Study Pavilion provides workspaces under, around and on top of its stepped structure.
cards.source_title: Fleet RISD Library – Fleet Library – architects
cards.access_notes: Inside Fleet Library; use during library access hours and follow library space policies.

cards.title: Fleet Library Living Room
cards.subtitle: Fleet Library, first floor
cards.notes: Bring a reading or sketchbook to the library’s named living-room area, a documented ground-floor gathering location.
cards.short_summary: A named first-floor library area suited to informal reading and reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD’s Unbound Art Book Fair identifies the RISD Library Living Room as a ground-floor area of Fleet Library.
cards.source_title: Exhibitor FAQ – Unbound Art Book Fair
cards.access_notes: Inside Fleet Library; current access is governed by library building hours and event setup needs.

cards.title: Fleet Library Study Terrace
cards.subtitle: Fleet Library, first floor
cards.notes: Choose the named study terrace for a change of setting, then keep materials compact so the shared area stays usable.
cards.short_summary: A documented first-floor study zone in Fleet Library.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD’s Unbound Art Book Fair identifies the RISD Library Study Terrace as a ground-floor area of Fleet Library.
cards.source_title: Exhibitor FAQ – Unbound Art Book Fair
cards.access_notes: Inside Fleet Library; current access is governed by library building hours and event setup needs.

cards.title: Fleet Library Study Area
cards.subtitle: Behind Circulation, Fleet Library first floor
cards.notes: Use this named study area behind the circulation desk when you need a defined library work zone near access services.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor study area positioned behind Fleet Library’s circulation desk.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD’s Unbound Art Book Fair identifies the RISD Library Study Area behind the circulation desk as a ground-floor location.
cards.source_title: Exhibitor FAQ – Unbound Art Book Fair
cards.access_notes: Inside Fleet Library; use during current library access hours and keep clear of circulation operations.

cards.title: Fleet Library Video Viewing Rooms
cards.subtitle: Fleet Library main hall
cards.notes: Plan media-focused research in the library’s documented video viewing rooms and confirm availability with library staff first.
cards.short_summary: Dedicated Fleet Library rooms for viewing-based research work.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD’s 2023 Architecture Program Report states that Fleet Library’s main hall includes video viewing rooms.
cards.access_notes: Availability and any use requirements are not stated in the report; confirm with Fleet Library before relying on a room.

cards.entity_name: Fleet Library Archives and Special Collections Reading Room
cards.title: Archives and Special Collections Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Fleet Library, second floor
cards.notes: Request collection-based research here when rare books, artists’ books or archival materials will shape your project direction.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor reading room for archival and special-collections research.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD documents a second-floor reading room for Archives and Special Collections at Fleet Library.
cards.source_title: Fleet Library | Rhode Island School of Design Research
cards.access_notes: Located on Fleet Library’s second floor; confirm reading-room access and collection-handling procedures with library staff.

cards.entity_name: Fleet Library Visual + Material Resource Center
cards.title: Visual + Material Resource Center
cards.subtitle: Fleet Library, second floor
cards.notes: Work from visual and material references here when physical samples and picture resources will sharpen a research question.
cards.short_summary: A Fleet Library resource space for hands-on visual and material reference work.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD states that Fleet Library contains a Visual + Material Resource Center and documents expanded visual and material resources on its second floor.
cards.access_notes: Within Fleet Library; ask staff about access to specific visual or material resources.

cards.title: Edna W. Lawrence Nature Lab
cards.subtitle: RISD campus research resource
cards.notes: Bring a drawing or research prompt and investigate forms, patterns and processes through specimens and imaging systems.
cards.short_summary: A nature-focused research environment with specimens and microscopy resources.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says the Nature Lab offers more than 80,000 preserved specimens, microscopy and micro-imaging systems, and equipment for studying specimens.
cards.source_title: Edna W. Lawrence Nature Lab | Rhode Island School of Design Research
cards.access_notes: Confirm current lab access, equipment use and any orientation requirements directly with the Nature Lab.

cards.title: RISD Museum Galleries
cards.subtitle: RISD Museum, Providence
cards.notes: Use the galleries for close-looking practice: select one object, sketch details and develop questions from its materials and context.
cards.short_summary: Collection galleries for visual study across art, design and decorative arts.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD states that its museum houses about 100,000 works and offers exhibitions, lectures, tours, workshops and resources for students and researchers.
cards.access_notes: RISD says faculty, staff and students are admitted free with ID; follow museum visitor policies for in-gallery study.

warnings: The Study Pavilion source is a third-party hosted copy of Fleet Library architectural documentation; all other cards use RISD-operated sources.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named Providence corridor stops within RISD’s practical orbit, each anchored by a documented arts, history, library, or performance destination.

cards.title: North Main Street: RISD Museum
cards.subtitle: North Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Approach via the documented 20 North Main Street entrance, then use the museum’s current visitor information to plan a gallery visit.
cards.short_summary: A museum entry point on the North Main Street edge of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD Museum directs visitors to enter through its 20 North Main Street entrance.
cards.access_notes: The source identifies the 20 North Main Street entrance and notes that both museum entrances and galleries are wheelchair accessible.

cards.title: Benefit Street: Providence Athenæum
cards.subtitle: Benefit Street corridor
cards.notes: Check in at the Visitor Center and take the self-guided tour through this historic library’s three floors during public visiting hours.
cards.short_summary: A historic library visit with self-guided exploration on Benefit Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Providence Athenæum is at 251 Benefit Street and invites non-members to explore its three floors with a self-guided tour.
cards.access_notes: Visitor information lists 251 Benefit Street, states that all are welcome, and asks visitors to check in at the Visitor Center.

cards.title: Power Street: John Brown House Museum
cards.subtitle: Power Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the rear visitor entrance described by the museum and reserve a timed visit if you want to explore Rhode Island history inside.
cards.short_summary: A documented historic-house museum on Power Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rhode Island Historical Society locates the John Brown House Museum at 52 Power Street and describes its public history interpretation.
cards.source_title: The John Brown House Museum | Rhode Island Historical Society
cards.access_notes: The museum lists its visitor entrance at the rear and directs visitors to purchase tickets in advance.

cards.title: Empire Street: AS220
cards.subtitle: Empire Street corridor
cards.notes: Check AS220’s current program before walking over; the Empire Street complex includes gallery, performance, studio, and youth-program spaces.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit arts complex occupying the Empire Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: AS220 identifies its Empire Street Complex at 95–115 Empire Street and lists galleries, performance venues, community studios, and its youth studio there.
cards.source_title: AS220: Create, Learn, Explore, Perform, Exhibit
cards.access_notes: AS220 lists weekday public hours of 10 am–6 pm; individual program spaces may have separate schedules.

cards.title: Washington Street: AS220 Mercantile Block
cards.subtitle: Washington Street corridor
cards.notes: Look for the Mercantile Block at 131 Washington Street and check AS220’s listings for public-facing fabrication, print, gallery, or event activity.
cards.short_summary: AS220’s Washington Street building for studios and making resources.
cards.evidence_claim: AS220 locates its Mercantile Block at 131 Washington Street and lists program studios including a fabrication lab and printshop.
cards.source_title: AS220: Create, Learn, Explore, Perform, Exhibit
cards.access_notes: The source identifies the building and its listed spaces; consult AS220’s current programming for visitor availability.

cards.title: Steeple Street: WaterFire Stage
cards.subtitle: Steeple Street corridor, between North Main and Canal
cards.notes: On a scheduled WaterFire night, walk Steeple Street between North Main and Canal to locate the organization’s outdoor performance stage.
cards.short_summary: A WaterFire performance-stage stop on the short Steeple Street link.
cards.evidence_claim: WaterFire identifies its Steeple Street Stage as located on Steeple Street between North Main and Canal.
cards.access_notes: The stage is associated with WaterFire events; verify the event schedule and performance lineup before going.

cards.title: Memorial Boulevard: WaterFire
cards.subtitle: Memorial Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Use WaterFire’s route guidance to walk the river parks along Memorial Boulevard during a scheduled lighting, rather than relying on one address.
cards.short_summary: A riverwalk-based public-art route along Memorial Boulevard.
cards.evidence_claim: WaterFire states that the installation takes place along Memorial Boulevard and the Providence and Woonasquatucket Rivers.
cards.access_notes: WaterFire says the installation spans more than a half mile in downtown river parks; confirm scheduled lighting dates before visiting.

cards.title: Westminster Street: WaterFire Ballroom
cards.subtitle: Westminster Street corridor at Weybosset Street
cards.notes: During a scheduled WaterFire Ballroom program, find the dance floor at the Westminster and Weybosset intersection and check event details first.
cards.short_summary: A documented temporary dance-floor site in the Westminster corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: WaterFire locates its Ballroom at 1 Turk’s Head Place/76 Westminster Street, at the intersection of Westminster and Weybosset Streets.
cards.access_notes: This is event programming rather than a permanently operating venue; confirm whether a Ballroom program is scheduled.

cards.title: Weybosset Street: The VETS Box Office
cards.subtitle: Weybosset Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the documented 220 Weybosset Street box-office location when you have selected an all-ages-appropriate performance on The VETS calendar.
cards.short_summary: The VETS’ event-day box office on Weybosset Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The VETS lists its on-site box office at 220 Weybosset Street and says it is open on event days.
cards.access_notes: The VETS states that its on-site box office is open only on the day of events; review the event’s age guidance before purchasing.

cards.title: Avenue of the Arts: The VETS
cards.subtitle: Avenue of the Arts corridor
cards.notes: Use the auditorium’s official calendar to choose an appropriate show, then approach the venue at One Avenue of the Arts on event day.
cards.short_summary: A major performing-arts destination on Avenue of the Arts.
cards.evidence_claim: Veterans Memorial Auditorium lists its address as One Avenue of the Arts, Providence.
cards.access_notes: Admission and access depend on the selected performance; the venue’s official calendar provides current event information.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented recurring RISD celebrations, showcases and rituals—each tied to the school’s student or academic community.

cards.title: Vote, make and wear a theme at Artist Ball
cards.subtitle: Annual October costume dance at RISD
cards.notes: Watch for the annual theme, then make a costume and join the runway competition, dancing and photo-booth festivities.
cards.short_summary: A student-themed costume celebration built around making and showing work.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD describes Artist Ball as an annual October costume dance where students vote on a theme, make costumes and walk a runway; it calls the event a RISD tradition.
cards.access_notes: Check RISD’s Involved calendar for the current event details.

cards.title: See Carr House become Haunted Haus
cards.subtitle: Annual October event at Carr House
cards.notes: Bring friends to the Campus Activities Board’s October transformation of Carr House, with a spooky walkthrough and candy.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Halloween-season Carr House transformation led with CAB.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says Haunted Haus is an annual October event in which Carr House turns spooky, hosted alongside the Campus Activities Board.
cards.source_title: Annual Student Events | RISD Student Hub
cards.access_notes: Consult the current RISD events calendar for date and entry details.

cards.entity_name: Care Week and Late Night Breakfast
cards.title: Start finals Care Week with Late Night Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Finals-period Student Life program at The Met
cards.notes: Use the finals-week kickoff at The Met, then choose from the calming activities, massages and therapy-animal events that follow.
cards.short_summary: A Student Life finals-week sequence centered on decompression and care.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD states that Care Week occurs during finals and starts with Late Night Breakfast in the Met, followed by calming activities, massages and therapy animals.
cards.source_title: Annual Student Events | RISD Student Hub
cards.access_notes: Current dates and participation details are posted through RISD’s Involved calendar.

cards.title: Meet makers at the Student Art Sale
cards.subtitle: Annual April sale at 20 Washington Place
cards.notes: Visit the April sale to see current students present work from their studios; purchasing is optional, so browsing is welcome.
cards.short_summary: A decades-running campus sale that foregrounds current student work.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD calls the Student Art Sale a campus tradition several decades running and says the annual event lets students showcase their work.
cards.access_notes: RISD lists the 2026 sale for April 18, noon–4 pm, at 20 Washington Place; verify future dates before going.

cards.title: Watch Apparel Design’s Collection runway show
cards.subtitle: Annual senior thesis show in Apparel Design
cards.notes: Look for the spring presentation to see graduating Apparel Design students debut their unified thesis bodies of work.
cards.short_summary: A recurring senior runway presentation that turns thesis work into a public show.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says that every spring Apparel Design seniors debut work in Collection, the department’s senior thesis show, and describes it as a longstanding annual fashion show.
cards.source_title: RISD Collection — Apparel Design Senior Thesis Show | RISD
cards.access_notes: Venue and attendance arrangements vary by year; check RISD event listings.

cards.title: Catch the FAV Senior Show
cards.subtitle: Annual Film / Animation / Video senior showcase
cards.notes: See graduating Film / Animation / Video students present their final films, or use the official page’s streaming links when offered.
cards.short_summary: A yearly showcase where FAV seniors premiere medium-spanning final films.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD calls the FAV Senior Show an annual tradition featuring work by graduating Film / Animation / Video students.
cards.source_title: Film / Animation / Video Department Senior Film Festival | RISD
cards.access_notes: Check the department’s current Senior Show page for program, venue and streaming information.

cards.title: Mark RISD’s March 22 founding through Founders Day
cards.subtitle: Annual March legacy celebration at RISD
cards.notes: Follow the March program for school-history events and service activities that connect RISD’s founding to its present mission.
cards.short_summary: A March commemoration of the women who founded RISD in 1877.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD states that it celebrates Founders Day in March with events and service activities honoring its entrepreneurial founders and legacy.
cards.source_title: RISD Founders Day | Community Celebration | RISD
cards.access_notes: Program elements change annually; confirm the current Founders Day schedule with RISD.

cards.title: Step into works-in-progress at Open Studios
cards.subtitle: End-of-semester RISD studio invitation
cards.notes: Plan a campus visit near semester’s end, when undergraduate and graduate students invite people into studios to see work in progress.
cards.short_summary: A recurring chance to encounter studio work before it becomes a finished presentation.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says that toward the end of every semester, undergraduate and graduate students invite people into RISD studios to see work in progress.
cards.access_notes: Dates, participating studios and visitor access vary by semester; check RISD’s event listings.

cards.title: View graduate thesis work at RISD Grad Show
cards.subtitle: Annual graduate thesis exhibition
cards.notes: Use the Grad Show to encounter final thesis bodies of work and celebrate the graduating graduate-student community.
cards.short_summary: A public-facing thesis exhibition marking graduate students’ completion of study.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD describes the RISD Grad Show as a public exhibition of final graduate thesis work that celebrates the graduate community’s achievements.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current exhibition dates, venues and visitor information through RISD before attending.

cards.title: Join the annual transition into RISD alumni life
cards.subtitle: RISD’s commencement ceremony in Providence
cards.notes: Follow current commencement programming to see RISD’s graduating class recognized alongside speakers, guests and the wider school community.
cards.short_summary: The school’s recurring degree-conferral celebration for its graduating community.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD reports that its 143rd Commencement on May 30, 2026 honored more than 700 undergraduate and graduate students receiving degrees.
cards.access_notes: Attendance arrangements and venue details are set for each ceremony; use RISD’s current commencement information.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Rhode Island School of Design, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented through RISD’s documented campus spaces, collections and student exhibitions.

cards.title: Start with a campus-landmark pause
cards.subtitle: RISD Beach · Benefit Street
cards.notes: Begin by locating the lawn between Waterman and Angell streets; use it as a simple outdoor checkpoint before exploring nearby buildings.
cards.short_summary: A named campus lawn for an easy first orientation stop.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD identifies RISD Beach as the grass on Benefit Street between Waterman and Angell streets.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus location; follow posted campus guidance.

cards.title: Get the campus layout in hand
cards.subtitle: RISD campus · Providence
cards.notes: Open the official map before choosing a route. It labels buildings, outdoor spaces, dining sites, galleries and key services across campus.
cards.short_summary: An official map anchors the rest of the weekend route.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD directs visitors to its online campus map for specific buildings and offices.
cards.access_notes: Available online; use the current map before traveling between sites.

cards.title: Browse the art-and-design stacks
cards.subtitle: Roger Mandle Building · 15 Westminster Street
cards.notes: Set aside time to see the circulating collection, artists’ books and Materials Resource Center; confirm entry and borrowing rules at the desk.
cards.short_summary: A documented campus library with extensive art and design resources.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says Fleet Library has a circulating collection of more than 150,000 books and includes a Materials Resource Center and artists’ books.
cards.access_notes: Check current library access and service hours before visiting.

cards.title: Look closely at the Nature Lab
cards.subtitle: Waterman Building · 13 Waterman Street
cards.notes: Visit with a specific visual question in mind, then ask staff about current access to the preserved-specimen collection and microscopy resources.
cards.short_summary: A RISD resource linking art, design and natural science.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD describes the Nature Lab as holding more than 80,000 preserved natural-science specimens plus microscopy and micro-imaging systems.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current hours and access procedures with the Nature Lab.

cards.title: Make time for the museum collection
cards.subtitle: 20 North Main Street / 224 Benefit Street
cards.notes: Choose a gallery or two rather than rushing the whole museum. Bring your RISD ID and check the museum’s current visitor information first.
cards.short_summary: A museum stop with free admission for RISD students carrying valid ID.
cards.evidence_claim: The RISD Museum states that RISD students receive free admission with valid college ID.
cards.access_notes: Current hours list Tue–Sun service; review closures and ticket guidance before arrival.

cards.title: See a current student exhibition
cards.subtitle: Chace Center, 2nd floor · 20 North Main Street
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition dates, then spend time with the show’s labels and installation. The gallery is a direct view of student-curated work.
cards.short_summary: A public-facing RISD gallery for student work and curatorial projects.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says the Gelman Student Exhibitions Gallery is accessible to museum visitors and the general public and offers student exhibition experience.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists Tues–Sun, 10 am–5 pm; confirm exhibition availability before going.

cards.title: Add Market Square to your bearings
cards.subtitle: Market Square · RISD campus
cards.notes: Use this map-listed campus space as a waypoint while connecting the downtown-facing buildings to the rest of the RISD route.
cards.short_summary: A named key space on RISD’s official campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD’s campus map lists Market Square among its key spaces.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor/shared campus space; observe any event setup or posted restrictions.

cards.title: Take a short outdoor reset
cards.subtitle: Farnum Park · RISD campus
cards.notes: Build in a brief stop at this named outdoor space, then use the campus map to decide whether to continue toward studios or downtown.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed RISD outdoor space for a route break.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD’s campus map directory identifies Farnum Park as an outdoor space.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space; check conditions and posted campus information.

cards.title: Trace another named outdoor space
cards.subtitle: Frazier Terrace · RISD campus
cards.notes: Use Frazier Terrace as a quiet map-reading stop. It helps turn a first walk through campus into a route you can repeat independently.
cards.short_summary: A documented outdoor waypoint on the RISD campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD’s campus map directory identifies Frazier Terrace as an outdoor space.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space; follow campus signage and any temporary restrictions.

cards.title: End near a map-listed patio
cards.subtitle: Metcalf Refectory Patio · RISD campus
cards.notes: Finish your walk by locating this named patio near the Refectory, then review the dining information separately if you plan to purchase food.
cards.short_summary: A named patio that closes the route near a campus dining building.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD’s campus map directory lists the Metcalf Refectory Patio among its outdoor spaces.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor patio location; dining purchases, if any, are separate.
